EXECUTIVE READOUT ON PASCAL BELAUD Concise Profile Pascal Belaud is the Chief AI & Data Officer (CAIO) at Truist Financial Corporation, having assumed this newly created executive position on November 24, 2025. 1 Reporting directly to Chief Information Officer Steve Hagerman, Belaud holds the enterprise mandate to shape the strategic vision and execution of Truist’s AI, data, and advanced automation initiatives. 1 Belaud’s appointment represents a significant pivot for the bank; he is a seasoned technology veteran with a 27-year tenure at Microsoft, where he spent 17 years in Microsoft France and the final decade in the New York office. 3 He culminated his Microsoft career as the General Manager of Cloud & AI Platforms for the U.S. Financial Services vertical, overseeing a group of more than 140 professionals, including cloud solution architects and data scientists. 4 Belaud holds a degree in Chemical Engineering from Toulouse and an Executive MBA from ESSEC Business School in Paris, and he characterizes his current position at Truist as "the mission of a lifetime in this AI era". 3 Likely Worldview Belaud’s operational worldview is fundamentally shaped by his extensive background in Microsoft’s "Customer Success" organization. 4 In enterprise technology, Customer Success divisions are measured not by code committed, but by actual platform adoption, business value realization, and the reduction of organizational friction. Consequently, Belaud views AI implementation as a challenge of process alignment and change management rather than a purely technical endeavor. He has publicly noted that 87% of data science projects fail, primarily due to a misalignment between the linear processes expected by corporate IT departments and the non-linear, iterative realities of data science. 6 Furthermore, Belaud is a proponent of "Accountable AI" and "Explainable AI." He has historically cautioned financial institutions against sacrificing accuracy for the sake of easily explainable, legacy models, arguing that such compromises leave "money on the table". 6 Instead, he advocates for sophisticated yet transparent architectures, such as Explainable Boosting Machines (EBMs), which satisfy regulatory requirements without compromising technological leverage. 6 Philosophically, Belaud favors augmentation over full automation. He introduced the concept of the "superworker"—a paradigm where AI functions as a "Mech Suit" for human employees, emphasizing that humans must remain deeply integrated within the loop to correct models and provide ground-level truth. 6 Likely Priorities At Truist, Belaud’s immediate mandate is to drive technological innovation at "speed and scale". 3 His organizational priorities revolve around generating operational efficiencies that simultaneously fuel revenue growth and elevate personalized experiences for both customers and teammates. 3 From an architectural standpoint, he is focused on standardizing AI deployment through "The Forge," Truist’s centralized AI operating model, which enforces strict governance, security, and observability standards. 8 A core priority will be moving AI initiatives out of isolated pilot phases and into "business as usual" enterprise operations, demanding measurable return on investment and seamless integration with existing business workflows. 10 What He May Care About Most in This Role Given the compensation band ($481K OTE) and the strategic positioning of the Head of AI Enablement role, Belaud is evaluating executive maturity and architectural translation capabilities. He will care deeply about the candidate's ability to operate as the critical diplomatic and technical bridge between the centralized AI function (The Forge, overseen by enterprise strategy) and the frontline operational realities of the Care Center (managed by Kimberly Dorsett). 8 Belaud requires assurance that the candidate can navigate the inherent tension between the rigorous, "production-first" standards of Truist's Azure-centric central AI operations 9 and the high-volume, latency-sensitive demands of the Care Center's AWS Connect environment. 13 His focus will be on validating the candidate's capacity to drive authentic frontline adoption, drastically reduce teammate friction, and deliver short-term metric improvements while simultaneously constructing the architectural foundations required for Charles Morris’s downstream "Agentic Enterprise" roadmap. 10 What Not to Overdo With Him The candidate must actively avoid over-indexing on fully autonomous "agentic" hype. Because Belaud's philosophy explicitly favors human augmentation and human-in-the-loop systems, presenting AI as an autonomous replacement for human agents will contradict his "superworker" framework. 6 Furthermore, the candidate must not present as a theoretical technologist who lacks business acumen. Belaud has witnessed the systemic failure of isolated data science teams and requires leaders who prioritize change management, cross-functional alignment, and concrete business metrics. 6 Finally, the candidate must avoid proposing massive, disruptive "rip-and-replace" strategies. Truist operates with the immense technical complexity inherited from the BB&T and SunTrust merger 14 ; dismissing this legacy debt rather than architecting elegant abstraction layers over it will signal a lack of enterprise pragmatism. The candidate must articulate how to build modern AI orchestration layers that interact with legacy systems via secure APIs. The strategy must focus on abstracting legacy complexity away from the frontline, delivering modern capabilities without requiring a massive "rip-and-replace." 7. Legal, Compliance, and Responsible AI Truist adheres to strict Responsible AI frameworks and recognizes that regulatory compliance is a major friction point, particularly concerning data privacy, PII handling, and AI-driven fraud mitigation. 18 Innovation cannot outpace risk controls. AI systems must be mathematically proven to be compliant, secure, and auditable before deployment. Compliance must be treated as a foundational design input, not a post-development hurdle. The candidate must emphasize pre-inference PII redaction, immutable observability patterns, and deterministic routing to ensure that the Care Center's AI workflows remain fully compliant. C. WHAT THIS FINAL 20-MINUTE INTERVIEW IS PROBABLY REALLY ABOUT At a compensation level indicating Senior Vice President (SVP) or equivalent seniority ($481K OTE), a 20-minute final interview with a C-suite executive like Pascal Belaud is rarely a tactical technical screen. Belaud is not assessing the candidate's ability to write Python code or configure an AWS Connect instance; he is executing a highly calibrated assessment of executive presence, strategic alignment, and organizational maturity. What Pascal is Likely Validating Belaud is validating whether the candidate possesses the diplomatic acumen and architectural vision to operate as a strategic peer. He is evaluating the candidate's capacity to straddle two distinct and often conflicting environments: the rigorous, highly governed, Azure-centric world of the central AI function (The Forge), and the pragmatic, high-velocity, metric-driven world of the Care Center. Belaud needs absolute assurance that the candidate can seamlessly translate Charles Morris's abstract, enterprise-wide agentic roadmap into Kimberly Dorsett's immediate, P&L-driven operational reality without causing organizational friction or violating enterprise governance standards.
